About the Game [There are real friends in the online world!] Doomed Otaku is a story-driven adventure game where a wandering 20-something Otaku travels between two worlds—reality and the internet—experiencing various incidents along the way. The protagonist, Jin Da-yeon, is a die-hard fan of the Japanese idol game, "Idol☆Star." Upon hearing that limited-edition character perfumes are launching in Japan, she ends up leading a group purchase for the merchandise. However, being terrible with money, she impulsively spends all the collected funds on personal expenses. Only 14 days left until the order deadline... Can she scrape together $5,000 in time to place the order? Face reality and reform... or escape to the internet and face doom? A full-blown immersive Otaku psychological thriller: Doomed Otaku !! Live faithfully in both reality and the internet to pay back the $5,000 ! In Doomed Otaku , reality is a dull and colorless world. In contrast, the internet world is vibrant and full of excitement. 1. Manage the Apartment! Help the landlord manage the apartment building! If you get close to the residents... you might receive unexpected help. 2. Explore Various Locations! Forget-Me-Not Village is filled with suspicious people and mysterious items. Search thoroughly for anything that might be worth some money! 3. Work at the Logistics Center! You can earn a daily wage by working at the logistics center near the apartment . Work hard (if you can)! 1. Spend a Happy Day with Idols! In the protagonist’s favorite game, "Idol☆Star," enjoy dates and play games with Ikeman, Neketsu, and Shotaro! 2. Intervene in Petty User Disputes! All sorts of incidents happen among the Otakus. They are waiting for you—the internet’s biggest superstar—to settle their drama! 3. …Is there a user who trades game money for real cash…? A user who trades "Idol☆Star" currency for real money?! Earn gold through in-game activities and convert your game money into cash! 1. SP (Social Point) As a shut-in, Da-yeon needs SP (Social Point) to go outside. If your SP runs out, you will no longer be able to take any actions. 2. Character Progression Relationships can be romantic, professional, or even toxic rivalries. Even characters who already have partners can be your target! Build connections in various ways and see what lies at the end of each path. 3. Multi-Ending & The Importance of Choice Experience over 20 different endings depending on the choices the protagonist makes. (Submarine Operators Not Actually Ready) is a 1–4 player co-op submarine sim where teamwork is essential, panic is inevitable, and sinking is always one wrong button away. Use sonar, pilot, fight, repair, and pray your friends know what to do. Join our community on Discord About the Game S.O.N.A.R. is a 1–4 player online co-op submarine simulator where teamwork is essential, panic is inevitable, and sinking is always just one wrong button away. Coordinate with your crew, use sonar to detect threats, and operate a cutting-edge submarine through combat operations, stealth infiltrations, and treasure recovery missions. Repair catastrophic malfunctions, recalibrate complex systems, and desperately hope that the person sitting next to you isn't just randomly pressing buttons. UNDERWATER MISSIONS The oceans are under enemy control. Gather a team of highly trained specialists (or at least people who claim they know what they're doing) and complete dangerous missions beneath the waves. - Locate hostile vessels with sonar and send them to the bottom of the sea. Preferably before they do the same to you. - Protect valuable cargo ships. Because apparently the military couldn't find anyone else to babysit them. - Hunt for treasures. Use sonar to search the ocean floor for lost riches, forgotten artifacts, and evidence of previous crews' poor decisions. - Slip past enemy destroyers undetected. Stay quiet. Stay hidden. And whatever you do, don't sneeze. COOPERATION Up to four crew members must work together to manage nine critical stations, including navigation, diving, sonar, periscope operations, engineering, and damage control. Your sonar operator tracks contacts while the rest of the crew keeps the submarine alive. When the sub catches fire or starts taking on water from twelve different holes at once, communication is the only thing standing between you and becoming fish food. Use proximity voice chat to: - Shout urgent orders. - Warn everyone about imminent disaster. - Explain why the catastrophe is definitely someone else's fault. And if a crewmate starts reading the manual during a torpedo attack, give ’em a friendly slap back to reality! Nothing says "successful mission" quite like a victory dance while all hell breaks loose. CUSTOMIZATION In S.O.N.A.R. every character is unique. Choose from dozens of uniforms, hats, and questionable fashion choices. Customize your equipment before deployment and unlock new gear as you level up. If you're going to make terrible decisions underwater, you should at least look good doing it. SURVIVAL Machines aren't the only things that break down. Humans do too. Manage your crew's food supplies, rest schedules, and overall well-being. Neglect them for too long and they'll become exhausted, seasick, delirious, or mysteriously incapable of following simple instructions. Health Tip: You really, really don't want to be vomiting inside your diving helmet when it's your turn to load the torpedoes. Trust us on this one.
